[MUQATIL:82:6-13/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Satan is what deluded the human being.

[TUSTARI:82:6/r1] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | What deludes a person is what cuts him off from God despite God's gentleness and generosity.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r10] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | Whoever remains in this reliance finds air, open space, earth, and sky all equal.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r11] TUSTARI, d. 283 · عمر بن واصل | reports | Sahl's disciple Umar ibn Wasil said that ignorance in leaving God's protection was what deluded him when he recited the verse.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r2] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | Nothing is nearer to the servant than the believer's heart; when something other than God enters it, that presence becomes a veil.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r3] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | One who beholds God with the heart becomes distant from everything besides Him.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r4] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | Whoever seeks God's good pleasure, He makes content through His forbearance.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r5] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | When someone surrenders the heart to God, God takes charge of the limbs and makes them upright.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r6] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | The heart's testimony reflects the degree to which a person has guarded the limbs.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r7] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | Keep the heart steadfast in awareness that the Creator is with His creatures, and persist in works because God watches wherever people are.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r8] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | Bring one's needs to God and remain at His door.
[TUSTARI:82:6/r9] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | Recognize one's ignorance, weakness, and incapacity while relying on God as the knower, strengthener, and able one.

[TAB-FULL:v24p177/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatada identifies the enemy that deluded Adam's son as Satan.

[THALABI:v10p146/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · الشاعر | reports | An admonitory couplet asks the sinner how he is unashamed when God is with him in private and says divine reprieve and concealment deceive him.

[THALABI:v10p146/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Ibn Masud reports that God will privately ask every person at resurrection what deceived him, what he did with his knowledge, and how he answered the messengers.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r10] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | Qushayri's couplet dramatizes the sinner's excuse: God's repeated generosity has emboldened him despite the Master's rebuke.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r7] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The question asks what deceived or misled a person into disobeying God.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r8] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | One prompted answer is that God's generosity emboldened the sinner: He saw and concealed, and could punish but granted respite.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r9] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | Another interpretation says a believer trusts God's beneficence and is deceived by prolonged respite; forbearance emboldens bad conduct despite the believer's presumption that a lapse was impossible.

[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r6] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The question asks what deceived a person into adorning falsehood and neglecting what God required.

[JISHUMI:v10p7309/r12] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Ghurūr is a delusive matter that makes someone ignorantly imagine safety from what should be feared.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r10] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · الكلبي ومقاتل | reports | Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say it was revealed about al-Aswad ibn Shariq, who struck the Prophet without immediate punishment; the verse asks what God's forbearance led him to assume despite disbelief.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r11] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says Satan, the enemy empowered over the person, deceived him.

[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r15] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · الفضيل بن عياض | reports | Asked how he would answer God, al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said God's lowered veils had deceived him.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r16] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · يحيى بن معاذ | reports | Yahya ibn Muadh says he would answer that God's past and present kindness had deceived him.

[TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Another definition says the Generous accepts a little and gives much.

[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r4] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أهل التفسير | reports | A third sense is forgiving or generous, as in the references to the gracious Lord.

[BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r10] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The question asks what deceived and emboldened a person to disobey; calling God generous is meant to deter presumption, since generosity does not require neglecting wrongdoers or equating obedient and disobedient people.

[BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | reports | The source notes two verses beginning يا أيها الإنسان, one asking what deceived the person about the generous Lord and one saying the person labors toward the Lord.
[BURHAN:v2p216/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | One mode of Quranic address is general address intended generally, illustrated by the call to humanity in 82:6.
[BURHAN:v2p318/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · قيل | reports | One view disallows marveling at God's act, since saying how great God is might suggest that something made Him great, whereas His attributes are eternal.
[BURHAN:v2p318/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · قيل | reports | Another view permits such language because magnifying God accords with worshippers' belief in His greatness and power; an anonymous poem says He can bring the distant near.
[BURHAN:v2p318/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · بعض المحققين | reports | Some scholars answer that astonishment magnifies the matter itself; it need not imply that another agent caused it, and its cause may simply be hidden from us.
